g.title: user
g.text: name · age 5-10 · something from today · a shelf (11 genres, Surprise me, My own idea)

g.title: guard
g.text: clean text · real names only · injection phrases

g.title: screen
g.text: Safety screen (LLM, only for "My own idea")
soften or block · original characters · genre

g.title: ideas
g.text: 98 seeds: a want · a funny obstacle · a twist
space & animal seeds: hero + a true fact

g.title: listener
g.text: a child of this age picks one pitch + why

g.title: library
g.text: the voice to copy, never the plot

g.title: head
g.text: prompt: HEAD_WRITER_SYSTEM + beats_prompt (with a worked example)
beat sheet: funny rule · 3 tries (plan → set-up → punchline → so next)
planted idea · solution · twist · running joke ×3 · last line

g.title: drafts
g.text: 3 DRAFT WRITERS, in parallel (LLM, each in two halves)
the library example is sent as their "own earlier story"

g.title: scene
g.text: rewrite or lengthen ONE passage, never new events

g.title: rehearse
g.text: one breath per sentence · long ones split in code

g.title: rails
g.text: finish only if safe, 500-800 words, reviewed and rehearsed
every refusal says why · 2 polish edits after a passing draft
stuck after 4 refusals · budgets: 22 tool calls, 90 s

g.title: out
g.text: STORY on the page: title page + pages, read aloud with the computer's own voice
(the agent's steps appear on the book's cover while it works)
The parent can ask for a change ("make it funnier"): checked for injection, fenced as <parent_change>,
and the same agent edits the story page by page with rewrite_passage → review_story → finish.

g.title: beatcheck
g.text: child is the hero · seed's twist & fact · age-safe

g.title: pick
g.text: the winning draft becomes the story

g.title: judge
g.text: → score computed in code → report card

g.title: double
g.text: keeps only real problems · fails closed

g.title: trace
g.text: every turn, prompt, reply and time
